finding.summary: The hardened helper callback used the owning TCM pointer after a conditional that initialized it only when the pending marker equaled 1.
stock_evidence: offline_static/ghidra_stock/decompiled/0165_00113590_syna_dev_helper_work.c derives the TCM base as work-0x528 only in the valid-marker body, then clears the pending word at work-8 and returns after either branch.

offline_static/stock_assembly/0165_syna_dev_helper_work_00113590.asm branches on the marker and reaches a shared epilogue that stores zero at work-8; no TCM pointer is used on the invalid-marker branch.
finding.reconstruction_issue: The C hardening moved pending clearing into syna_dev_helper_work_complete(tcm), but left the TCM pointer assignment inside the marker condition. The unconditional completion call therefore received an indeterminate pointer when the condition was false.

change.mechanism: Derive tcm as work-1320 (0x528), matching the stock owner offset, before evaluating the pending marker. The shared completion helper then clears pending state under its existing spinlock on both paths.
change.behavior: The callback still performs reset handling only when the low marker byte is 1. The false-marker path still clears pending state and returns, now with a valid owner pointer.
change.classification: HARDENED_STOCK_DEVIATION; lifecycle locking remains, and the owner derivation now safely covers the stock shared epilogue path.

limits: No kernel runtime, workqueue state injection, Android boot, or NX809J hardware execution was performed.
The invalid-marker path was reviewed statically; no runtime fault-injection harness was run.
